battle.name: 法國武裝干涉墨西哥
battle.theater: 維克薩斯港與墨西哥中部高原
battle.brief: 一八六一年十二月，法國、西班牙與英國聯軍自維克薩斯港登陸墨西哥，藉口追討外債並重建秩序；此役歷時五年半，法軍節節推進攻入首都，扶植馬克西米連稱帝，最終被墨西哥與美國聯手逼退。加特林機槍此時方問世，僅少量流入帝國軍與北方邊防，戰局勝負仍由步砲與補給線決定。

countries: 墨西哥共和政府與法國遠征軍是這場衝突的兩大交戰主體，旁邊還有始終觀望的美國。共和國一方：一八六一年十二月聯軍在維克薩斯港登陸當日，總統胡阿雷斯·貝尼托·華雷斯宣佈中斷與三國的外交關係，隨後當選共和國總統；軍隊由聯邦軍、國民警衛隊與各州民兵組成，總司令先後為伊格納西奧·岡薩雷斯與華雷斯本人，關鍵戰將則有伊格納西奧·薩拉戈薩、波菲里奧·迪亞斯、萊奧納多·馬爾克斯等。帝國一方：一八六四年四月，哈布斯堡家族的馬克西米連在墨西哥城加冕，翌年頒布帝國憲法，米格爾·米拉蒙出任「皇帝代理人」主持帝國政務；帝國軍以保守派的改革軍為骨幹，另招募奧地利、比利時、德國與義大利志願兵組成外籍法團。法國方面組建遠征軍團，初期約六千人，一八六二年由讓·皮埃爾·巴贊接任指揮，一八六四年由弗朗索瓦·福雷接替並晉升元帥，一八六七年卡諾貝與卡斯特爾諾先後率增援接掌。西班牙派出約一千二百人，由佩塞盧埃拉將軍率領；英國海軍霍普准將只帶了七百名水兵與海軍陸戰隊，駐紮維克薩斯港周邊，一八六二年四月即行撤走。美國自始保持中立：不承認帝國，卻在戰後向共和軍輸送軍火。
countriesEn: The two principal belligerents were the Mexican Republic and the French expeditionary corps, with the United States standing beside them as a third party that never entered the war. On the Republican side: on the very day the allied column landed at Veracruz in December 1861, President Benito Juárez severed relations with the three powers and was then elected President of the Republic. His armed forces combined the federal army, the National Guard and the state militias, under a supreme command that passed from Ignacio González to Juárez himself, with the field commanders who mattered most being Ignacio Zaragoza, Porfirio Díaz and Leonardo Márquez. On the imperial side: in April 1864 the Habsburg prince Maximilian was crowned in Mexico City, and in the following year the empire received its constitution, with Miguel Miramón appointed as the emperor's proxy and head of the imperial government. The imperial army rested on the conservative Reform troops and on foreign volunteer formations recruited from Austria, Belgium, Germany and Italy. France organized a special expeditionary corps: about six thousand men in the first echelon, with command passing to Jean-Pierre Bazaine in 1862, to François Forey in 1864, and in 1867 to Canrobert and then Castelnau as reinforcements arrived. Spain sent some twelve hundred men under General José de la Pezuela. Britain sent only about seven hundred bluejackets and marines under Rear-Admiral James Hope, and after the battle of Puebla in April 1862 they withdrew entirely. The United States never fought in Mexico: it refused to recognize the empire, yet supplied the Republican government with arms once the American Civil War was over.
people: 關鍵人物分三層。決策層有法國皇帝拿破崙三世，他力主出兵並把墨西哥視為帝國秩序的試驗場；外交層有美國國務卿威廉·西沃德，他自一八六五年起主張法軍撤出墨西哥；國家層有墨西哥總統胡阿雷斯·貝尼托·華雷斯，他在流亡中仍主持政府，堅持共和國的法統與暫停償還外債不變。對應的戰場指揮官：法軍一八六二至一八六四年由巴贊指揮，一八六四至一八六六年由福雷指揮，一八六七年初由卡諾貝接任，六月卡斯特爾諾率增援抵達墨西哥城並主導撤退談判；帝國軍由米拉蒙與費利克斯·蘇洛亞加掌舵，外籍法團則由奧地利籍與比利時籍指揮官率領。共和軍一端最關鍵的是薩拉戈薩，一八六二年五月五日靠民兵與幾個營的守軍在普埃布拉拖住法軍，使「五月五日之戰」成為共和國的象徵。波菲里奧·迪亞斯以游擊與機動作戰拖住法軍，一八六七年率軍奪回普埃布拉，又在瓜達拉哈拉擊敗帝國聯軍，隨後晉升為共和國將軍，最終在一八七六年成為總統。岡薩雷斯任總指揮，馬爾克斯主持墨西哥城防務並在城破時率殘部向西部撤退。另有由美國南部解甲黑人志願兵組成的維吉尼亞兵營，編入共和軍，在墨西哥本土與帝國軍交過手。
peopleEn: Three layers of people shaped this war. At the level of decision-making sat Napoleon III, who pressed for the intervention and treated Mexico as a proving ground for a European order in the Americas; and William H. Seward, United States Secretary of State, who from 1865 demanded that the French army leave Mexico. At the level of the Mexican state sat Benito Juárez, who kept his government alive in exile and refused to abandon either the republican legality or the suspension of foreign debt payments. The commanders matched them one for one: the French corps was led by Bazaine from 1862 to 1864, by Forey from 1864 to 1866, and in 1867 by Canrobert, with Castelnau arriving in Mexico City in June to negotiate the withdrawal. The imperial side was run by Miramón and Félix Zuloaga, with the foreign legions officered largely by Austrian and Belgian commanders. On the Republican side the decisive figure was Ignacio Zaragoza, whose few battalions and civic guards held the field at Puebla on 5 May 1862, turning the engagement into a republican emblem. Porfirio Díaz harried the French with mobile columns and irregular warfare, retook Puebla in 1867, beat the imperial coalition at Guadalajara, and rose to the rank of general and, decades later, to the presidency. Ignacio González directed the armies in the field, and Leonardo Márquez commanded the defence of the capital and led the remnants west when the city fell. A place of their own belongs to the Battalion of Virginia, black volunteers from the American South who enlisted in the Republican army and fought imperial troops on Mexican soil.
kits: 任務單這件加特林機槍是全場最年輕的裝備：它由理查德·喬登·加特林在康乃狄克州哈特福德造出，一八六〇年前後定型，一八六一年在美國公開演示，一八六二年南北戰爭中才首次見於戰場。進到墨西哥的數量極少：帝國政府曾向美國廠商訂購成批的加特林機槍，主要配給北部索諾拉、奇瓦瓦一帶的邊防部隊，用來對付阿帕奇與雅基游騎隊的襲擊，也有一部分留作首都與維克薩斯港的守備；法軍遠征團是否配發同型機槍，文獻記載零星且互相矛盾，不宜視為主力火力。所以在本戰役的火力體系裡，加特林機槍只是新技術的試用件，真正決定攻守的仍是傳統火炮：法軍有十二磅與二十四磅阿爾貝特式野戰炮，攻城時用大口徑海軍重炮配合坑道、炸藥與突擊；墨軍以史密夫一八六一年式五八口徑步槍為骨干，輔以來復槍、佩德森後膛步槍與少量老式火槍。運輸靠騾隊、鐵路與維克薩斯港的船隊，內陸最後一段由便攜窄軌鐵路與人力接駁。
kitsEn: The Gatling gun named in the task sheet is the youngest piece of equipment in the entire campaign. Richard Jordan Gatling built it at Hartford, Connecticut; the design was settled around 1860, the weapon was demonstrated publicly in 1861, and it saw combat for the first time during the American Civil War in 1862. Only a handful reached Mexico. The imperial government ordered Gatling guns in small batches from American manufacturers, and most of them were allocated to the northern frontier in Sonora and Chihuahua, where they were used against Apache and Yaqui raiders; a few were kept for the defence of the capital and of Veracruz. Whether the French expeditionary corps itself was issued Gatling guns is recorded only in scattered and contradictory sources, and it cannot be treated as a main source of firepower. In the fire system of this war the Gatling gun was therefore an experimental novelty. What actually decided attack and defence was traditional artillery: the French brought twelve- and twenty-four-pounder Albert-pattern field guns, and for the sieges used heavy naval guns together with saps, mines, powder and assault. The Mexican army was built on Springfield Model 1861 rifles of .58 calibre, supported by Sharps repeating rifles, Pederson breech-loading rifles and a few obsolete muskets. Transport rested on mule trains, the railway and the shipping out of Veracruz, with a portable narrow-gauge line and human muscle handling the final leg inland.
tactics: 法軍的戰術核心是「工程兵開路、港口設點、逐州推進」。維克薩斯港一登陸便設營壘、囤積糧秣、修築堡壘與船塢，遠征團以港口為後方，用手推砲與艦砲控制海面，再沿維克薩斯至哈瓦卡至普埃布拉的縱深公路與後來鋪設的鐵路向北推進，補給由船隊運到港、騾隊接駁到前線。一八六三年從普埃布拉向墨西哥城的攻勢歷時約四十日，靠沿途築路、徵發與架橋維持；縱隊分散、宿營設寨，每到一地先取水源與高地。一八六七年攻墨西哥城則集中重砲於查普特佩克要塞西北角，以大口徑海軍砲日夜轟射牆基，再以地雷炸開缺口，要塞終於在六月十三日淪陷。共和軍的戰術相反：主力避開法軍野戰砲的正面，轉入山區與鄉村打游擊，破壞鐵路、橋樑與驛站，切斷首都與港口之間的補給；一八六七年改採圍城與夜襲，迪亞斯在普埃布拉以奇襲奪城，岡薩雷斯在墨西哥城以游擊隊與圍城同時施壓。帝國軍被夾在中間，多依賴法軍砲兵掩護與外籍法團的攻堅。總結：這是一場以補給線長度決定勝負的消耗戰，旋轉機槍在此毫無意義。
tacticsEn: The French method was to let the engineers open the road, fix the ports and advance state by state. On landing at Veracruz they entrenched, stockpiled food and ammunition, and built redoubts and a dockyard; the expeditionary corps treated the port as its base, covered the sea with light guns and naval artillery, then pushed north along the Veracruz-Jalapa-Puebla axis, later supported by the railway, with food and ammunition unloaded from the ships at the harbour and carried forward by mule teams. The advance from Puebla to Mexico City in 1863 took some forty days and was sustained by road building, requisitions and bridging along the way; columns were dispersed, camps were fortified every night, and every objective was taken first for its water and its heights. The attack on Mexico City in 1867 concentrated the heavy guns on the north-west angle of the Chapultepec citadel, battering the wall day and night with a heavy naval gun and finally detonating a mine under it until the breach was opened and the citadel fell on 13 June. The Republicans did the opposite: they kept the main body away from the French field artillery, took to the hills and the countryside, and cut the railway, the bridges and the relay stations that linked the capital to the port. In 1867 they switched to siege and night attack, Díaz storming Puebla in a surprise assault while González pressed Mexico City with guerrillas and a blockade at the same time. The imperial army was caught in between, leaning on French gun cover and the foreign legions for its attacks. In the end this was a war of attrition decided by the length of the supply line, and the rotary machine gun had no place in it.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下：一八六一年十二月首批聯軍約六千名法軍、一千二百名西班牙兵與七百名英國水兵及海軍陸戰隊。一八六二年五月五日普埃布拉之戰，法軍出動約六千人，傷亡被俘約一千二百人，共和軍陣亡數百人。戰後法軍兵力續增，一八六四年遠征軍在編約兩萬上下，一八六七年卡諾貝與卡斯特爾諾兩批增援抵達後，駐墨法軍與隨軍人員總數常被估為接近四萬。共和軍則由一八六二年初的數千人擴張到一八六七年約兩萬人。裝備面：墨西哥在一八五八至一八五九年間向美國購得約一萬五千支史密夫一八五五式步槍，一八六六年美軍又交付約一萬五千支佩德森後膛步槍，但多數未及上戰場。距離與交通：維克薩斯港至普埃布拉的鐵路一八六三年通車，全線約三百七十公里；普埃布拉至墨西哥城公路約二百一十公里，最後一段靠騾隊與便攜窄軌鐵路銜接。城市規模：一八六三年九月法軍入城遊行時出動約二萬人，首都人口當時約十七萬。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. In December 1861 the first allied force comprised about six thousand French soldiers, some twelve hundred Spaniards and about seven hundred British bluejackets and marines. At the battle of Puebla on 5 May 1862 the French engaged with roughly six thousand men and lost, killed, wounded or captured, about twelve hundred, while the Republicans lost several hundred dead. French numbers kept growing: the expeditionary corps numbered about twenty thousand men in 1864, and after the reinforcements of Canrobert and Castelnau arrived in 1867 the total French military and civilian personnel in Mexico was often estimated at close to forty thousand. The Republican army, a few thousand strong at the start of 1862, grew to around twenty thousand by 1867. On equipment, Mexico had bought about fifteen thousand Springfield Model 1855 rifles from the United States in 1858 and 1859, and in 1866 the American army delivered about fifteen thousand Pederson breech-loading rifles, most of which never reached the front. On distance and transport, the railway from Veracruz to Puebla opened in 1863 along a route of some three hundred and seventy kilometres; the road from Puebla to Mexico City ran for about two hundred and ten kilometres, with mule teams and a portable narrow-gauge line bridging the last stretch. For scale: when the French paraded through the capital in September 1863 they put roughly twenty thousand men on the street, and the city then held about one hundred and seventy thousand inhabitants.
cause: 起因有三層。第一層在墨西哥自己的政治：克里奧爾政府一八五三年垮臺後，改革派依一八五七年憲法與改革法令推行土地與教會改革，觸動克里奧爾、軍官與地主的利益，一八五七至一八六一年的改革戰爭中保守派軍隊屢敗，最終與改革派達成一八六一年十月三十日的塔庫巴亞協定，等於把國家權力交到共和派手上，也把整批不滿的保守派軍官推向外人。第二層是債務：一八六一年十月墨西哥宣佈停付外債三十三年，維克薩斯港海關收入無法再抵押給英法荷三國債主，倫敦、巴黎與阿姆斯特丹的金融損失無數。第三層是國際形勢：美國內戰牽制了華盛頓，倫敦金融界主張出兵，巴黎則懷著在美洲建立帝國的算盤，拿破崙三世想證明法國能改造一個大國的政局，並藉此分散歐洲因德意志統一而來的注意力。於是一八六一年秋，巴黎以三國債主利益受損為名，邀西班牙與英國同行，製造出「歐洲集體維護債務」的姿態。
causeEn: There were three layers of cause. The first lay inside Mexico: after the Creole government fell in 1853, the reformists governed under the 1857 constitution and the reform decrees touching land and the Church, which cost them the backing of the clergy, the officer corps and the landowners; the conservative armies lost the Reform War of 1857 to 1861 and finally accepted the Tacubaya agreement of 30 October 1861, handing the state over to the republicans and pushing a resentful corps of conservative officers toward foreigners. The second cause was debt: in October 1861 Mexico declared a thirty-three-year suspension of foreign debt payments, and the customs revenue of Veracruz could no longer be pledged to the British, French and Dutch creditors, so the financial claims of London, Paris and Amsterdam went unpaid. The third cause was the international situation. The American Civil War tied Washington down, financiers in London argued for intervention, and Paris dreamed of building an empire in the Americas: Napoleon III wanted to prove that France could reorder the politics of a great power, and to distract Europe from the coming unification of Germany. So in the autumn of 1861 Paris invoked the interests of the three creditor states, called in Spain and Britain, and manufactured the appearance of a European collective action to protect debts.
impact: 影響至少延伸到三個方向。對墨西哥：華雷斯政府在最危急時退到美國邊境甚至遠赴華盛頓求援，反而因禍得福，讓「墨西哥人的墨西哥」成為美洲政治的新命題；一八六七年二月頒布的胡阿雷斯法廢除教會特權與軍人特權，為後來的世俗共和國鋪路；波菲里奧·迪亞斯在戰爭中崛起，帝國崩潰後由他接管國家，墨西哥此後長期走向開放外資與歐美貿易的路線。對美國：內戰結束後華盛頓有了餘力，羅斯克蘭斯受命主持對墨交付軍火，謝里登先後赴墨考察，聯邦政府以「不承認帝國、承認共和」為由向巴黎施壓，門戶開放與門羅主義因此得到一次實戰式檢驗，帝國垮台也讓歐洲列強重新估算干預美洲的代價。對歐洲與軍事技術：這場戰爭是歐洲正規軍與新式旋轉火力在美洲的第一次大規模對照，馬克西米連的帝國常被視為歐洲軍制輸出的失敗樣本；同時也讓加特林機槍這類新武器的推廣速度受制於補給與財政，一八六〇年代已存在的旋轉機槍在墨西哥幾乎沒有存在感。
impactEn: The consequences ran in at least three directions. For Mexico: driven to the American border and even to Washington, Juárez turned disaster into advantage, and Mexico for the Mexicans became a new political formula for the Americas; the Juárez law of February 1867 abolished the privileged courts of the Church and the fuero militar, paving the way for a secular republic; Porfirio Díaz rose through the war and took over the country after the empire fell, leading Mexico for decades towards an open policy for foreign capital and trade with Europe and the United States. For the United States: with the Civil War over, Washington had the strength to act, Rosecrans was charged with delivering arms to Mexico, Sheridan went to the country on mission, and the federal government pressed Paris with the twin formula of refusing to recognize the empire and recognizing the republic, so that the open-door policy and the Monroe Doctrine were put to a practical test; the collapse of the empire also forced the European powers to price the cost of intervening in the Americas. For Europe and for military technology: this war was the first large-scale comparison in the Americas between regular European armies and new rotary firepower, and the Maximilian empire is often read as a failed sample of European military export. It also showed how quickly the spread of a new weapon such as the Gatling gun could be throttled by supply and finance, since a rotary machine gun already existing in the 1860s left almost no trace in Mexico.
result: 結局是法軍全面撤退。一八六七年四月，迪亞斯部攻入普埃布拉；五月五日，帝國皇帝馬克西米連在克雷塔羅遭共和軍擊敗並被俘，六月十九日於克雷塔羅被處決（所謂「將軍，再見」一語出自後世小說，並非史料記載）。六月十九日卡斯特爾諾率增援抵達墨西哥城，隨即與共和政府達成索萊達德協定：法軍在七月與八月分批由維克薩斯港登船，最後一批法軍於一八六八年才離港。帝國政權隨之崩解，蘇洛亞加與米拉蒙先後流亡，華雷斯回到首都重掌政權，普埃布拉的「五月五日」後來成為墨西哥最重要的國家紀念日之一。加特林機槍在這場戰爭裡沒有留下決定性痕跡：它隨帝國軍的少量訂購在北方邊防上試用過，卻沒有出現在任何決定戰局的交會中；真正把法軍拖垮的，是數百公里長的補給線、永無止境的土木工程、急速膨脹的軍費，以及一支不斷消耗、士氣低落的遠征軍。
resultEn: The French withdrew completely. In April 1867 Díaz's men stormed Puebla; on 5 May the emperor Maximilian was beaten at Querétaro and captured, and on 19 June he was executed there, the famous farewell to the general being a later literary invention rather than a historical record. On 19 June Castelnau's reinforcements reached Mexico City and the convention of Soledad was concluded with the Republican government: the French embarked in July and August, and the last French troops left the port of Veracruz only in 1868. The imperial regime collapsed with them, Zuloaga and Miramón went into exile, Juárez returned to the capital, and the Cinco de Mayo of Puebla became one of the proudest national anniversaries of Mexico. The Gatling gun left no decisive mark in this war: it was tried in small numbers on the northern frontier with the imperial army and appeared in none of the engagements that decided the outcome. What wore the French down was the length of a supply line running for hundreds of kilometres, endless engineering works, a rapidly swelling military budget, and an expeditionary army that was slowly consumed and steadily losing heart.
